question.text: In the SEBI-prescribed PPM template, what is the key difference between Section VIII for a Category I/II AIF versus a Category III AIF?

answer.text: Cat I/II Section VIII covers 'Principles of Portfolio Valuation' while Cat III Section VIII covers 'Determination of the Net Asset Value of Units' — reflecting illiquid valuation vs NAV-based valuation
Cat I/II Section VIII is about tax treatment while Cat III is about leverage
Section VIII is identical for both; the difference is only in Section IX
Cat I/II don't have a Section VIII at all

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.5 Box 13.1, Section VIII for Category I/II AIFs is 'Principles of Portfolio Valuation' (covering Valuer details, valuation frequency, IPEV Guidelines). For Category III AIFs, Section VIII is 'Determination of the Net Asset Value of Units' (covering NAV computation, valuation policy, Valuation Committee role). The distinction reflects the illiquid/private nature of Cat I/II versus the liquid/mark-to-market nature of Cat III. The Trap: Tax and leverage are separate sections. Section VIII is NOT identical. Cat I/II do have Section VIII — the content differs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B distributor exams test categorisation. XIX-C requires drilling into the template's category-specific sections. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a Cat I/II fund, adopt IPEV Guidelines explicitly in your PPM and IMA — becomes your valuation defense if a write-down is challenged by any LP later.
